title: Two pointers: opposite ends
learn: left/right moving inward, needs sorted input or symmetric property, pair-sum logic
hook: Two Sum II, 3Sum, Container With Most Water and Valid Palindrome are all interview classics, and all the same move: start at both ends and let each comparison throw one element away.

explain.prompt: Explain the two-pointer technique on a sorted array, and why it finds a pair with a target sum in O(n) without missing any pair.
keyPoints: pointers start at both ends and move toward each other
sum too small → move left (the smallest can't pair with anything); too big → move right
each step eliminates one element for good, so no valid pair is skipped
O(n) time, O(1) space; needs sorted input or a symmetry
